definitions.gloss: tedious talk, pretentious excuses, long-winded complaints
definitions.explanation: Self-important or tiresome talk, especially complaints, excuses, or justifications that others find annoying. Almost always used in the negative expression 御託を並べる (to spout tedious excuses).

examples.japanese: {御託|ごたく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{並|なら}べる→並べる：01091_naraberu⟧な。
⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦いつも→いつも：00599_itsumo⟧{御託|ごたく}⟦ばかり→〜ばかり：02006_bakari⟧⟦{並|なら}べている→並べる：01091_naraberu⟧。
{御託|ごたく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{並|なら}べていないで→並べる：01091_naraberu⟧、⟦さっさと→さっさと：05795_sassato⟧⟦{仕事|しごと}→仕事：00480_shigoto⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{始|はじ}め⟦なさい→なさる：01307_nasaru⟧。
examples.english: Stop making excuses and get to work already.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost exclusively used in the set phrase {御託|ごたく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{並|なら}べる→並べる：01091_naraberu⟧ (to line up pretentious talk = to make tedious excuses or complaints). The word carries a dismissive, impatient tone toward what someone is saying. Originally from Buddhist terminology referring to oracles or divine pronouncements ({御託宣|ごたくせん}), the modern usage is ironic — treating someone's talk as if they think their words are as important as divine proclamations.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {御託|ごたく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{並|なら}べる→並べる：01091_naraberu⟧: to spout excuses, to go on and on
- {御託|ごたく}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧: enough with the excuses
